Haruki Murakami, What I Talk About When I Talk About Running (2007) -- his own memoir

discipline.rationale: In his own words to The Paris Review: "When I'm in writing mode for a novel, I get up at four a.m. and work for five to six hours... I keep to this routine every day without variation" -- a specific, self-described, sustained daily discipline, not an inferred work ethic.

deep_focus.rationale: In his own words, described repetition itself as "a form of mesmerism. I mesmerize myself to reach a deeper state of mind" as part of his sustained daily writing routine -- a specific, self-described method for achieving concentrated creative focus.

independent_thinking.rationale: Directly connects his physical training (running one marathon a year, six miles most days, never taking more than two consecutive rest days) to his writing practice in his own words: "Most of what I know about novel writing, I learned by running every morning on the road" -- a specific, self-articulated, unconventional theory of his own craft.

planning_orientation.rationale: Described a fixed, invariant daily schedule -- writing hours, running or swimming, reading, and a 9 p.m. bedtime -- maintained without exception during novel-writing periods, per his own account to The Paris Review.
